section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes the findings of a single study that investigated how college women's exposure to body-focused and non-body-focused others impacts their body image and eating behavior. The study found that interactions with non-body-focused others uniquely predicted more adaptive body image outcomes both between- and within-persons, while exposure to body-focused others predicted more maladaptive outcomes at the between-persons level. The section also explores potential explanations for these findings based on social learning theory and suggests avenues for future research.
